methodology.score: (player losses + 0.5 * draws) / resolved fights; timeouts excluded from score, retained separately
methodology.labels: Within each edition/stage/gameDifficulty, tied score groups share their midpoint percentile and the same quartile label. Score=1 is VERY_HARD, score=0 is EASY. Saturated pools may have fewer than four labels; no ID tiebreak can create an unsupported difficulty distinction.
methodology.player: Purchasable base forms within edition and current shop tier, unique families where possible; random, 3-unit synergy, full synergy, upper-half base-stat draft; legal merge trees through native GameLoop.moveUnit with documented copies budgets. Permanent rewards use the exact native reward table and application logic. No spending/economy simulation.
limitations: Equal mix of budgets and roster styles is a reference distribution, not measured player behavior. Each global difficulty is calibrated separately.
Fixed progression contexts and difficultyScore=turn; losses can shift real progression.
Infinite rosters draw from legal edition possibilities; do not model per-run unlock draft restrictions.
Ranks near boundaries or tied scores have low certainty; a four-way split is a UI ranking, not statistical separation.
methodology.economy: Every purchase costs 3 gold. Team copies are capped at floor(turn*10/3), never exceeding cumulative natural income (10 per turn); the strongest budget may spend up to this ceiling, leaving no guaranteed reroll allowance. Unusable copy budgets remain unspent. This is a stat/merge budget ceiling, not a modeled probability of assembling the roster. Lower budgets leave income unspent. Merges use actual GameLoop logic, exp 3/9 star thresholds, native evolution and merge effects; no artificial stat growth.
methodology.parity: Headless receives the same enemy multiplier, capStats and psychic arguments as the live engine. Paired tests reset battle RNG to the same seed. Full labels use live BattleSimulator regardless of parity results.
methodology.playerRewards: Budget 0: no permanent rewards; budget 1/2/3: one actual NORMAL/HARD/EXTREME PERM_SYNERGY reward per prior win, applied with native GameLoop.applyPermanentReward. Select the reward synergy matching most current units, seeded ties. Assumes the current roster survived and benefited throughout; these are hypothetical valid reward histories, not measured player distributions. No extra flat stats or hand-authored reward values.
methodology.legalMerges: Every merge passes native moveUnit with identical family/name and both levels below 3. Evolved sources are built from their own base copies through legal merges. Three-star units stop accepting copies. Unusable copy budget is not purchased or charged. A five-slot scratch board keeps two actual allied units and up to three synthesis units; native merge effects affect the allies actually present. The other two final allies are assembled outside this scratch context. Eevee evolves with native weights from those two allies and stops after its first evolution, rather than assuming another Eevee independently evolves into a matching form. Every source/target/result exp, form, level and copy count is saved in mergeHistory.
methodology.rewardAvailability: A unit receives historical rewards only after its original shop tier could first appear: T1/T2 turn1, T3 turn3, T4 turn6, T5 turn10. One prior win is assigned to each earliest historical turn. No guarantee is made about exact rolls, purchases, or reward offers; these are stage-budgeted benchmark scenarios.
methodology.preparation: Player startBattlePhase invokes native prep-end synergies and individual effects exactly once for the current turn. Native refreshSpecialDescriptions assigns enemy charmander/pichu/riolu N=max(1,wins). Player growing skill N and Psychic N remain 1 and 2 respectively, without inferred past history.
